game.intro: The moon borrowed Joel's sneakers and went for a jog. Pick fast, guess faster.
game.question: If you had to sprint somewhere right now, where would you most like to end up?

game.intro: Somebody warmed the bench for you. Sit down and point your camera at something cozy.
game.prompt: Something soft you would happily sit on for an hour. Get close enough to count the threads.

game.intro: Focus day. Saturn has one question and zero patience for correct answers.
game.question: How do bees make honey?

game.intro: Don't even scream: you drew the same doodle. Now prove your ears are just as synced.
game.prompt: The noise your favourite doodle would make if it came to life. The other guesses the doodle.

game.intro: Gemini moon, forty tabs open, zero regrets. Close one by explaining it in emoji.
game.prompt: The last random thing you looked up out of pure curiosity.

game.intro: A hermit crab moved into a bigger shell and threw a party. Bring three stories; one is from nowhere.
game.prompt: Three places you have lived or stayed that had a strange quirk. One quirk is made up.

game.intro: The fog mailed you a postcard. It says: decide quickly, I roll back in at noon.
Leo moon: the Tiger meets a lion cousin at the family reunion. Pick your big-cat move.
game.question: You meet a long-lost big cat cousin at a reunion. What's your opening move?

game.intro: Today everything gets a standing ovation. Even the tiny stuff. Especially the tiny stuff.
game.prompt: Something ordinary you used today that deserves applause. Zoom in on its finest feature.

game.intro: Virgo moon. The sock drawer is under audit, and Saturn wants answers. Preferably wrong ones.
game.question: Why do socks come in pairs?

game.intro: DES: two strangers said Saturn on the same day. The judge is flattered. Make some noise for him.
game.prompt: What Saturn's rings sound like spinning. Hum, whoosh or rattle, but commit.

game.intro: Libra moon, and the playground seesaw is in delicate talks. One word breaks the deadlock.
game.headline: PLAYGROUND SEESAW REFUSES TO GO UP AGAIN UNTIL IT GETS ___

game.intro: The lupins held a vote and they want poetry. Saturn counts the lines. Guess without going over.
game.question: How many lines are in a traditional sonnet?
game.source: A sonnet is by definition a 14-line poem (Petrarchan 8+6, Shakespearean 4+4+4+2)

game.intro: Scorpio moon and a locked drawer nobody mentions. Answer before your curiosity picks the lock.
The black flies called a summit. You did not RSVP. Negotiate anyway.
game.question: The black flies offer peace if you give up one outdoor June thing. What do you trade away?

game.intro: The moon is clearing its throat before a big speech. Show us its stunt double.
game.prompt: Something round that has sat in the same spot for ages. Get close enough to see its craters.

game.intro: Archer's Full Moon Recharge. Ruby and onyx are on the sill. Aim your wrong answer at the bullseye.
game.question: What does an archer aim at?

game.intro: Unplanned detour day. Saturn has rerouted the whole show through your voice memos.
game.prompt: A GPS voice recalculating after a wrong turn, in pure noises. No words allowed.

game.intro: Don't even scream: ladders everywhere today. Climb Nancy's mountain one emoji at a time.
game.prompt: Something you would find at the very top of a tall place.

game.intro: Full moon on Nancy's mountain, spotlight on. Tell three, fib once, and watch who blinks.
game.prompt: Three times you got a cheer or a round of applause as a kid. One never happened.

game.intro: Longest day of the year, so naturally this is the shortest round. Ten seconds each, solstice star.
Nancy's half-birthday is officially recognized. Saturn ordered half a cake. Choose wisely.
game.question: What is the correct way to celebrate a half-birthday?
options: Half a song, sung very loudly

game.intro: Aquarius moon wants weird inventions. Show us a gadget so close it looks like it came from space.
game.prompt: Anything with buttons, dials or switches. Get close enough that it looks like a spaceship console.

game.intro: Tide pool daydream. Nothing to do but stare at tiny crabs and answer badly.
game.question: Why does the tide go in and out?

game.intro: The fog forgot its lines and is just mumbling now. Help it out with a sound effect.
game.prompt: A sea creature making a dramatic stage entrance: seal, whale, lobster or crab. Give it a noise.

game.intro: A bottle washed up with no message inside. The front page needs to know what was in there instead.
game.headline: BOTTLE WASHES ASHORE WITH NO MESSAGE, ONLY A TINY ___

game.intro: DES: an orange cat at exactly 4:07. Saturn is obsessed with clocks today. Guess carefully.
game.question: How many minutes are there in one full week?

game.intro: Moon in Aries, Tiger at the starting line. One sprint, three pairs, no warm-up lap.
Taurus moon says lie down. The hammock is open to negotiations. State your terms.
game.question: The hammock will hold you all afternoon, but you may bring only one thing. What is it?

game.intro: June is folding its beach towel and heading home. Show us a little summer before it goes.
game.prompt: Something striped: towel, umbrella, shirt, awning. Zoom in until the stripes look like a highway.
